notes.title: Saviour of the Wastelands is now live!
notes.notes:
​It's finally here! I've been working on this game on and off in my spare time for far longer than I care to think about! It started out as a minigame idea for my other project, but quickly ballooned into something way beyond it's original scope. Normally, going way beyond the scope of your idea is a terrible thing to do, as you can easily lose yourself in ideas that'll never come to completion. But, I really enjoyed the story that came out of this, and wanted to make it into something proper.

So, here we are! Saviour of the Wastelands! I'm so glad it's finally available for people to play! I had so much fun making this, coming up with the storylines, adding little easter eggs and references to my other project and how the two tie together! I just hope you enjoy playing it as much as I enjoyed making it!

notes.title: V1.0 is now live!
notes.notes:
It's done, Episode 1 is officially "complete". I say complete in quotes, because knowing me, I've missed something and there will definitely bugs that need fixing. If you've played V0.26, then you've played all the content there is in Episode 1. V1.0 is simply a polish on existing content, marking the end of development of Episode 1.

I did update some older renders, as well as updating a few animations, so if you're interested in playing again, it'll at least look much better! Episode 2 will be going live soon, which will continue the story right where Episode 1 left off. Speaking of which, what did everyone think to the ending? Let me know, but try to avoid posting spoilers!

I really hope you enjoyed Episode 1, it was a strange project to work on as it was originally only meant to be a learning project, but it some how evolved into a whole game. I have a habit of doing that, that's how Saviour of the Wasteland came into existence...

Anyway, thanks for playing and I hope you stick around for Episode 2!

notes.title: V0.26 Release!
notes.notes:
[b]V0.26 Release![/b]

Well, this arrived far faster than I expect, the ending of Episode 1! This is a huge milestone for both the game and myself. When I first started creating Lunar's Chosen, I never thought it'd reach the size it did, both in terms of the amount of content and popularity. If you're wondering by the way, I checked the total amount of dialogue for Episode 1 while looking into translating the game, there's over 484k words of dialogue! That's just dialogue, not code or anything else, just purely the bits you read in the in game text box. That's an insane amount of words!

Anyway onto the update, this update includes the ending of Episode 1, as well as more story for each of the main characters. It has a whole new location, the movie theatre, where you can take each of the main characters on a date once you unlock it, resulting in 9 new repeatable scenes! Speaking of repeatable scenes, I also updated Claire's footjob animation to be an actual animation!

Unrelated to content, I've also added a new feature in that you can name your save files. Most players don't really use this, so it's off by default, but if you want it, it can be toggled on in the preferences menu. 

Finally, to address why this is V0.26 and not V1.0 despite being the ending of Episode 1, that's because V1.0 will come later to Itch and Steam. It won't contain any new content, but there's a few things I want to give an additional layer of polish before I call it the official release build.


[b]Changelog:[/b]

- 12 New story scenes

- New location: cinema!

- 9 New repeatable scenes

- 3 New secret images

- Ability to toggle on/off naming saves (Default is off, can be found on the preferences menu)

- Remade Claire's footjob repeatable scene with new animations.

- Added the final scene! 

- Fixed a whole bunch of typos!

notes.title: Going Episodic
notes.notes:
Hi there!

As some of you have noticed, Lunar's Chosen recently changed name to Lunar's Chosen Episode 1. I know some people hate when games go episodic, but there are good reasons for me doing so and I want to take some time to explain to you the reasoning behind it. This is going to be a long wall of text, so strap in!

First of all, the code is a mess. I started this game originally as a learning project. It was never meant to be something that was out and about in public as a real game. As such, it's extremely poorly coded and that poor code prevents me from doing a lot of cool things I want to do, which I'll get to later. Could I recode it and tidy everything up? Sure, but it'd be a huge project and take a long time. If this was the only reason to go episodic, I wouldn't bother and would take that time to recode it, but there are other reasons too.

Build size. This is a weird point to have and doesn't apply to you guys on Steam, but I also release the game on other platforms and one of the main complaints I have from them is that the game is growing big to download. Certain hosts have a limit to the amount of data you can download in a day and many users hit that cap and can't download the game. This isn't a huge problem, until you look at the android build. I already crunch the hell out of it and it's starting reach the file size limit. Going episodic helps relieve both of these issues.

Speaking of the size of the game, it has grown far beyond what I originally planned. As I said above, this game was originally a learning project. It was meant to be short, teach me the basic and then left alone. Somewhere along the way people started really enjoying it and asking for more, so I obliged. Then I was told to put it on Steam and I did, but I didn't think the quality or the quantity was worth charging for so it was free. Then people said they'd pay for it and I added a load more content, so it gained a price. 

It was still intended to be finished long ago, but as I kept working on it, kept going back and improving the quality of older content and just had more and more to add so it's still going. Which is one of the reasons why I'm okay with making the game episodic. I don't personally feel like I'm cheating anyone out of content with episode 1, since there's already way more content than originally planned. That said, all of the above isn't enough reason alone for me to go episodic, there's also some huge benefits which I'll talk about now.

First, we have the code. As I mentioned, it's a mess and wasn't set up in a smart way. Neither were the scenes or the content flags. One of the main complains I get about content choices is how often the game asks you if you want to do something you've already said yes or no to. Another is if you play with futanari on, suddenly the game is filled with them. What if you wanted more control?

That's where being able to build episode 2 from scratch comes in. I can create preferences where players can control exactly what content they see far more than they do now. Want Amy to be the only futanari character? You can do that. What about if you want Amy and Leanne to be futanari, but not Meg? Sure you can do that too. What about gender swapping? Not into you're character being turned female, but you're fine with body swapping with one of the female characters? You can do that too. 

On top of that, tidying up the code makes the game far easier to manage. Right now I waste a lot of time trying to figure out where, how and why I wrote something the way I did and then figuring out how I need to write something new to make it work with what I created before. It's just a mess.

This would also allow me to implement some changes to the game that I've been wanting to do, but would complicate the code even more if it were added into the current code. So I'd be able to add new things that are currently too tricky for me to spend time on.

Next is translations. I get a lot of requests for translations of the game, but since I'm still working on this version, constantly adding, changing and fixing things, any translation would would also need to be changed or those players would get a lesser version. So right now, I'm not getting them done. If the came is complete though and going to be unchanged, it would be much easier to get translations created.

Achievements! Everyone loves achievements, but most also hate when achievements are taken away from them or changed. As it is right now, I can't put any "final" achievements into the game such as "sleep with every character" because what if I add a new character you can sleep with? Going episodic gives me an end point for the episode and allows final achievements to be added, which is much more satisfying for players. 

Finally, let's talk about money. "Aha! See! It's just greed! I knew it!" Let me just stop you there and say no, it's not greed, if it were, then every side character who isn't important to the main story, such as Fran, Hillda, Ellie, etc would have all been DLC you had to buy. Hell, I've just recently told players in my discord I won't add more content for them as DLC as, if I'm making episode 2, new content for them would go into that as it'd feel scummy to take content that should be part of the main game and purposefully leave it out to sell as DLC.

I am looking into if it's possible to give players who bought Episode 1 a steep discount on Episode 2. No idea if it's possible, but it's an avenue I'm looking into.

So hopefully this has given you some insight into the major reasons why the game is becoming episodic and shown you that it's not just some greedy cash grab. I know some of you won't be convinced and that's fine, frankly before I started doing this and learning what was involved, I'd have likely thought the same thing so I don't blame you. But hopefully most of you reading this can see the huge benefits of an episode 2.

Oh and don't worry, Episode 1 isn't ending just yet, there's still content to come!

If you made it this far, thank you for reading this wall of text and I hope you continue to enjoy playing the game as much as I enjoy making it! 

PTGames.

notes.title: V0.23 Release - The Achievement Update!
notes.notes:
V0.23 is here for everyone! This is a bit of a different update from usual as for the first time since the game was created, I'm encouraging people to start a clean save!

Why am I encouraging this? Because of achievements! A lot of achievements are granted as you progress through the game, so continuing an old save means you will be unable to get these achievements.

That said, if you're not interested in achievements, old saves should work fine, but save files have moved!

If you want to continue an old save, you'll have to go to the old save location C:\Users\%userprofile%\AppData\Roaming\LunarsChosen-1549893754 and move them to the new one which should be C:\Users\%userprofile%\AppData\Roaming\RenPy\PTGames\Lunars Chosen. Similar changes should be made to MAC and android save locations.

Of course, if you are starting a new save, you don't need to worry about that as the game will automatically save and load in the new location!

Additionally, there's also some revamped renders and animations in the early game too! For those of you that don't want to find all the secret images again or would like a bump start on money, there are cheat codes available for supporters over on Patreon.

notes.title: Price change complete and new Donation DLC
notes.notes:
As you may or may not have seen in the last announcement, Lunar's Chosen is no longer free. Unfortunately if you missed it while it was free, you will now need to buy the game if you wish to play. For now the price is not planned to change, but may be review in future or on full release of the game.

For those of you who got the game for free, you will still be able to play as normal. Many of you asked for a way to support the game beyond the wallpaper DLC. As such, there is now a donation DLC available for purchase on the game's store page. Please note that this DLC provides [b]ZERO[/b] content for the game, it is purely a way for those people who wish to support the game to do so.

notes.title: A price change
notes.notes:
This is just a quick announcement to say that with the release of V0.21, I'm now happy with the amount of content within the game to warrant putting a price on it. As such, after the 30th of September, 2022, the game will no longer be free.

So, if you were on the fence about trying the game, this is your warning to grab it now while it's free! Everyone who owns it, (even if you've never played it as long as it's in your library), [b]will keep the game after the price change[/b]. So if you get it now, it's yours to keep!

This also applies to those of you that already own it, don't worry, [b]it won't cost you anything to keep playing and receive future updates[/b]. Hopefully by making this announcement and giving you time to get it before the price changes, no-one will be upset with the game no longer being free.

Edit: It appears Steam have removed the button to add the game to your library from the store page earlier than planned during the transition to becoming a paid game. Unfortunately this is out of my control and I cannot say whether it'll be back before the 1st of October, but it may already be too late to grab the game for free! I have no control over this I'm afraid.

V0.21 is now here! This update contains a whole bunch of new early game scenes with whole new characters (don't worry, you don't need a new save to see them) as well as new story content for all the main characters. There's also new repeatable events, even animated ones! 

One of the most common complaints I get is about the lack of things to do in the early game, so I put it to a poll on Patreon and they decided that this update should focus on adding in some early game events. So now there are six new characters to meet and interact with. They won't have any major story like the main characters, but give you something to do in the early game between main story events. I plan on adding a couple more in each update going forward to really flesh out the world of the game.
